newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgium's Clabecq workers back rescue plan.
newsitem.headline: Belgium's Clabecq workers back rescue plan.

text.p: Workers at the failed Belgian steelworks Forges de Clabecq voted on Saturday in favour of a plan for Italian-Swiss firm Duferco to complete a partial takeover of the company, said Belgian news agency Belga.
The vote was by a unanimous show of hands, Belga said,
"This takeover does not resolve all our problems," FGTB union leader union Roberto D'Orazio told a meeting of workers.

He said problems included questions relating to back pay which workers say is due to them from the Walloon regional government, a redundancy programme for those workers not re-employed in the new enterprise and early retirement provisions.
D'Orazio called on Walloon politicians to act, warning of fresh problems for the regional government if they failed to reply clearly to workers' demands.

Clabecq filed for bankruptcy after the European Commission banned the southern Belgian region of Wallonia in December from injecting 1.5 billion Belgian francs ($41 million) into the loss-making firm and ordered the company to reimburse subsidies already granted.
Clabecq has appealed the Commission's decision before the European Court of First Instance.
The Walloon region, Clabecq's largest shareholder, and Italian-Swiss firm Duferco agreed earlier this month on a partial takeover of the company.
